comparisons.peer_summary: The total fair value of time-based RSUs vested was $2.0 billion in 2024, $1.1 billion in 2023, and $889 million in 2022, with $2.6 billion of unrecognized compensation expense remaining as of December 28, 2024, to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.63 years.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose the aggregate fair value of restricted stock units (RSUs) and performance share units (PSUs) that vested during the fiscal year. NVDA reports a total fair value of $8.2 billion for the year ended January 28, 2024, while AMD reports $2.0 billion for time-based RSUs vested in 2024. Both disclosures provide comparative figures for the prior two years, allowing for direct trend analysis of vesting values.

sentences.text: The total fair value of RSUs and PSUs, as of their respective vesting dates, during the years ended January 28, 2024, January 29, 2023, and January 30, 2022, was $8.2 billion, $4.3 billion, and $5.6 billion, respectively.
The total fair value of time-based RSUs vested during 2024, 2023 and 2022 was $2.0 billion, $1.1 billion and $889 million, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, the aggregate fair value of vested time- and market-based RSUs was $14,914 million, $5,423 million, and $4,207 million, respectively, based on the market value of common stock on the vesting date.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and AVGO both report the aggregate fair value of vested equity awards (RSUs and PSUs/stock options) in Item 8. NVDA reports $8.2 billion in fair value for RSUs and PSUs vesting in FY2024 (ended Jan 28, 2024). AVGO reports $14,914 million (approx. $14.9 billion) for time- and market-based RSUs vesting in fiscal year 2024. Both disclosures use the fair value at the vesting date as the metric.

sentences.text: The total fair value of RSUs and PSUs, as of their respective vesting dates, during the years ended January 28, 2024, January 29, 2023, and January 30, 2022, was $8.2 billion, $4.3 billion, and $5.6 billion, respectively.

The aggregate fair value of time- and market-based RSUs that vested in fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022 was $14,914 million, $5,423 million and $4,207 million, respectively, which represented the market value of our common stock on the date that the RSUs vested.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value estimation methods for equity awards
comparisons.peer_summary: The fair value of RSUs and PSUs with service or performance conditions is estimated using the common stock grant date value, reduced by the present value of expected dividends. PSUs with market conditions are valued using a Monte Carlo simulation model based on historical volatility.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA discloses the actual fair value of vested RSUs and PSUs ($8.2 billion). Intels (INTC) discloses the methodology for estimating the fair value of these same awards (RSUs and PSUs), stating they use the common stock grant date value reduced by dividends. While NVDA provides the executed financial impact of vesting, INTC provides the valuation assumptions for the awards, which is a related but distinct aspect of stock-based compensation disclosure.

sentences.text: The total fair value of RSUs and PSUs, as of their respective vesting dates, during the years ended January 28, 2024, January 29, 2023, and January 30, 2022, was $8.2 billion, $4.3 billion, and $5.6 billion, respectively.

We estimate the fair value of RSUs and PSUs with a service condition or performance condition using the value of our common stock on the date of grant, reduced by the present value of dividends expected to be paid on our shares of common stock prior to vesting.
We estimate the fair value of PSUs with a market condition using a Monte Carlo simulation model as of the date of grant using historical volatility.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capitalized stock-based compensation and unrecognized compensation costs
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 2024 and 2023, $99 million and $88 million of stock-based compensation expense was capitalized and remained in inventory, respectively. Unrecognized compensation costs for unvested awards were $1.44 billion as of August 2024, expected to be recognized through Q4 2028 with a weighted-average period of 1.2 years.
comparisons.comparison: While NVDA reports the total fair value of vested RSUs and PSUs ($8.2 billion), Micron (MU) discloses the amount of stock-based compensation expense capitalized into inventory ($99 million) and the total unrecognized compensation costs for unvested awards ($1.44 billion). Both disclosures address stock-based compensation costs and vesting activity, but NVDA focuses on the realized value of vested awards, whereas MU focuses on capitalized costs and future recognition obligations.

sentences.text: The total fair value of RSUs and PSUs, as of their respective vesting dates, during the years ended January 28, 2024, January 29, 2023, and January 30, 2022, was $8.2 billion, $4.3 billion, and $5.6 billion, respectively.
Stock-based compensation expense of $99 million and $88 million was capitalized and remained in inventory as of August 29, 2024 and August 31, 2023, respectively.

As of August 29, 2024, $1.44 billion of total unrecognized compensation costs for unvested awards, before the effect of any future forfeitures, was expected to be recognized through the fourth quarter of 2028, resulting in a weighted-average period of 1.2 years.
